name: How do project managers handle subcontractors on commercial jobs?

mainEntity.name: How does a commercial project manager coordinate subcontractors effectively?
mainEntity.text: How does a commercial project manager coordinate subcontractors effectively?

acceptedAnswer.text: Subcontractor coordination is one of the most important parts of commercial project management. Each trade depends on others, so the manager has to sequence work logically and monitor who is ready, who is delayed, and what materials are still outstanding. Regular coordination meetings, short-term look-ahead schedules, and clear site rules help reduce trade conflicts. The manager also needs to verify that subcontractors understand scope boundaries, access limits, inspection requirements, and quality standards. On Los Angeles-area jobs, coordination can be even more sensitive in occupied buildings or tight urban sites where deliveries and staging space are limited. Good project managers keep written records of commitments and follow up quickly when a trade slips. That level of control helps prevent one subcontractor’s delay from cascading through the entire project.
acceptedAnswer.description: They coordinate subcontractors by sequencing the work, confirming deliverables, holding progress meetings, tracking material lead times, and resolving trade conflicts before they affect the schedule. Clear communication and written commitments are essential to keeping multiple trades aligned.
